options.label: Different gateway
options.evidence: Leaving through Nhava Sheva instead of Chennai changes both the inland run and the sailing: road goes from 703 km to 21 km, saving 404 kg; 702 km of rail is added, adding 0.42 kg. Most of the difference is the road leg, which is charged per truck run rather than per tonne, so the distance driven is the whole of it. The workbook already sails Nhava Sheva → Laem Chabang 33 times and runs that inland chain on 62 shipments, so both halves of this route are ones it has already used.

options.label: Different inland route
options.tagline: Same gateway and sailing, a different run to the port
options.evidence: Same gateway, same sailing — only the run to Chennai changes. The road leg goes from 703 km to 645 km, saving 34 kg at 0.5928 kg CO₂e per km whatever the load. The workbook runs this shorter chain on 7 shipments (FY21-22), so it is a route the business has already used, not a proposal.

options.label: Different sailing
options.detail: Shorter sea routing — 5,002 km instead of 6,384 km
options.tagline: Same two ports, a different recorded sea route
options.evidence: The workbook records two different sailing distances for Chennai → Laem Chabang: 5,002 km on 7 shipments, against 6,384 km on this one — 1,382 km less at sea. The whole change is the ocean leg: at 0.0084 kg CO₂e per tonne-km on 60 kg, that is 0.70 kg saved. Same two ports, same gateway, and the inland run is untouched.
